answer: The design leans on staked peer review with spot checks, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. A basalt of per-task receipts records who did what, and the lagoon of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The trellis of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short.
